cells.tense: Here, with the pen — you're the one seeing what matters, and you're acting from it now.
cells.verb: Clearing away what was only pretending to be solid
cells.place: In the quiet knowing that tells you what deserves your attention
cells.ask: Offer one more piece of steady practice than feels safe — the kind that flows without forcing, where being alone with it connects you instead of cutting you off, and where getting better serves your growth rather than your grip. When practice stops straining, the knowing stays clear and you keep choosing what matters without having to defend the choice.
cells.core: You're seeing what matters and acting on it before you can explain why. The false supports have fallen — not because you tore them down, but because they couldn't hold what you already knew. What's left standing is truer, and you're standing in it. The next thing this clear sight is free to feed: practice that doesn't strain, solitude that keeps you close to people, refinement that makes you more rather than more clenched.
cells.sheetLine: You clear what can't hold, and you trust what you see.

cells.tense: Bracing against a future you're already trying to force open — the shattering has to happen *now*, before anyone can stop it.
cells.verb: Breaking things apart before they've had a chance to stand
cells.place: In the knowing that's become a hammer, unable to let anything stay whole
cells.ask: Let one thing stay standing this week. Hand over what you've learned to someone who can carry it forward — teaching that adapts, belonging that doesn't ask anyone to conform. When the meaning moves between people instead of being torn down ahead of time, the clearing stops costing everyone the ground they're standing on.
cells.core: You're clearing structures that haven't failed yet. Somewhere ahead is the version where everything false is finally gone, and you're living there — so every conversation, every plan, every quiet moment becomes a chance to dismantle. But chaos isn't the same as liberation. The structures you're breaking are still holding something, and the people inside them are getting buried in the rubble you're making. The clearing you want is real. It just isn't yours to force on this timeline.
cells.sheetLine: You're shattering what hasn't failed yet, and calling it freedom.

cells.tense: Still standing at a door that's already behind you — holding up what stopped holding.
cells.verb: Keeping dead structures upright with your own hands
cells.place: In the knowing that got scared and went quiet
cells.ask: Put one thing back into workable shape — not rigid control, just a container clear enough that things make sense in your presence. A structure that serves what it organizes. Build that and the current comes back through you: the knowing returns, and you'll see what to let fall because you'll finally have a place to stand while it does.
cells.core: You know something needs to fall, and you're holding it up anyway. Letting it go cost more than you could pay, so you learned to keep the walls up yourself — even after they stopped being walls and started being weight. The knowing hasn't left. It's just that holding something together with your bare hands doesn't leave a hand free to point at what's next.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding up what stopped holding, and your hands are full.

cells.tense: Pen down in a room you're already writing — the clearing is happening, but you're calling it something else.
cells.verb: Watching structures fall and calling it bad luck
cells.place: In a knowing that's steering without saying so
cells.ask: Name one thing you've been calling a collapse and start calling it what it is — something you already saw couldn't last. Then let the direction come from what you actually feel about it, not from the story that it's happening *to* you. Movement from genuine engagement is what returns; the ground stops feeling like it's moving under you and starts feeling like ground you chose.
cells.core: You already know what's about to fall — you've known for a while. You can feel it every time the subject comes up, every time you pause before answering. But you keep describing it as a surprise, or as something being done to you, or as chaos that arrived from outside. The knowing is running. The claim on it isn't. You're the one clearing the ground. You just haven't signed your name to it.
cells.sheetLine: You already know what's falling. You're still calling it a surprise.

flags.detail: "a while ago" — a cell knows no one's past
